page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The processor supports hyper-threading with 2 threads per core, a 33 MB L3 cache, and instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results position the n2-standard-8 primarily in the average tier for general computing tasks. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests falls within the middle 50% of tested systems, as do memory bandwidth speeds, which reach 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations, Redis SET operations at 7.12 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 6.9 GB/sec also demonstrate average performance. However, certain multi-threaded and specialized tasks, such as bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, Geekbench multi-core execution, and LLM prompt processing for small models, register in the lower 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-effective choice for stateless applications. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including moderate database operations, web serving, software compilation, and basic text processing tasks.
